subject: Pilot onramp decision: hosted evaluation vs private — quickstart & capacity asks
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Shah <amira@finlytics.com>, Finlytics DevOps <ops@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot onramp decision: hosted evaluation vs private — quickstart & capacity asks

Hi Amira / Finlytics team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the candid product-use context. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can scope the right pilot: Hosted API quickstart vs Dedicated/Private.

Summary (from our call):
- Primary goal: customer-facing summarization & transaction tagging in production within Q3.
- Non-prod workload can tolerate hosted sandbox; prod needs data residency discussion.
- Current traffic signal: ~25k monthly requests today, expected bursty peaks up to ~80 rps during end-of-day batch windows.

Our recommended quickstart (Hosted API):
- Provision sandbox endpoints (staging.+redwoodapi.com) for integration and validation.
- Start with a per-endpoint rate cap of 100 rps (burstable) + token-based billing; we can lower for specific routes.
- Enable KV prefix caching for repeated customer prompts to save tokens.
- Keep option open to move to Dedicated if sustained throughput >200 rps or strict VPC requirement.

Open asks for you (so we can finalize the pilot playbook):
1) Confirm expected steady-state qps and peak concurrency for the first 30 days (average and 95th percentile).
2) Any strict data residency / on-prem constraints for prod? If so, which region or legal requirement triggers Private deployment?
3) SOC2 / security review contact (security@finlytics or similar) — Marcus will follow up with docs.

Attachments: pilot-mpam-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet to capture traffic & endpoint mapping)

Proposed next steps:
- If ok, we send a 2-week hosted sandbox plan + quickstart checklist and schedule a 30-min infra sync to align on rate caps and latency SLOs.

I’ll follow up with Marcus on the technical play and a suggested load-test window.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Rep | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onramp decision: hosted evaluation vs private — quickstart & capacity asks

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. Quick answers from our side:

1) Traffic profile: steady-state ~900 q/d (queries per day) today (~1.5 qps average), but expected growth to ~5k q/d in month 1 of pilot. Peak bursts: up to ~80 rps for short windows (30–90s). 95p concurrency unknown — ops will estimate.
2) Data residency: prod-facing PII must remain in US regions; non-prod can be hosted. We don’t need on-prem unless legal flags it.
3) Security contact: security@finlytics.com (I’ve CC’ed them in a separate thread). Would appreciate your SOC2 + encryption-at-rest/KMS notes.

Budget/finance question: can you provide a rough cost ballpark for 100k queries/month with 200 tokens avg per query? We want to validate against our forecast.

Attachments: adding Ops contact for concurrency estimate.

—Amira
Amira Shah
Head of Product, Finlytics
amira@finlytics.com

Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onramp decision: hosted evaluation vs private — quickstart & capacity asks

Thanks Amira — that helps a lot. High-level responses and immediate next steps:

- Residency: Hosted in our US region satisfies the US-only requirement for prod (we’ll document region and egress contracts). If you later need a VPC/private deployment we can scope that (it’s common to start hosted → Dedicated → Private).

- Cost ballpark: I’ll send a topline estimate after Marcus shares expected token/time profile — rough back-of-envelope: ~USD 1k–3k/month for 100k short queries depending on model and caching. We’ll provide a more precise estimate with caching factored in.

Proposed quickstart plan (what we’ll deliver):
1) Sandbox endpoints (staging) with an initial 100 rps limit and burst policy (detailed by Marcus).
2) A one-hour infra sync next Wed to confirm concurrency and run a short load test.
3) Deliver SOC2 + KMS notes and the trial ops playbook (PDF).

Attachments: redwood-trial-ops-playbook.pdf — Marcus, can you confirm the exact burst window and token-throttling guidance we should communicate to Finlytics?

Best,
Kimberly
[Attachment: redwood-trial-ops-playbook.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 18:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onramp decision: hosted evaluation vs private — quickstart & capacity asks

Hi Amira / Finlytics ops team — Marcus here (solutions engineering). Quick technical primer and recommended controls for the hosted pilot:

- Endpoint mapping: split routes for (a) short-summary (avg token len 150) and (b) long-extraction (avg token len 800). Separate endpoints let us tune rate caps per route.
- Initial limits: Recommend 100 rps steady per route with burst to 150 rps for 60 seconds (allows end-of-day spikes). We can raise if telemetry shows steady higher throughput.
- Caching: Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated customer prompts — expect 20–40% token reduction on repeated patterns.
- Load testing: We can run a controlled 30-min ramp test from our staging agents; please provide an IP allowlist if you want to restrict test sources.
- Latency SLOs: For short-summary route expect p50 ~80–120ms per token on our US hosted nodes; we'll surface p95 in the infra sync.

Action for Finlytics ops: share a 2-hour window this week (or next Wed) for the sync + a primary contact to receive the test plan.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
